title: Sauteed Fresh Maize
author: Maama Nakato
desc: Kernels cut off ten fresh cobs and cooked twenty to thirty minutes with ginger, garlic, carrot and green pepper until every kernel goes translucent and the pan smells savoury.
longDesc: This is a father's signature recipe, made only when there is an abundance of fresh maize, and it is the kind of dish that only exists because of a glut. Fresh maize off the cob cooked slowly with aromatics develops a flavour the author describes as naturally meaty, which sounds like an exaggeration until you have cooked it for half an hour. Translucent kernels and a savoury smell in the air are the two cues, and they arrive together.
ingredients: 10 fresh ears of maize, or 720 ml (3 cups) kernels
A handful of green onions, finely chopped
steps: Cut the kernels off the cobs with a sharp knife and set them aside.
Over medium heat, add oil to the pan and wait for it to get hot.
Add the garlic, ginger and onions and let them brown a little.
Add the salt and tomatoes and let the tomatoes soften.
Add the maize kernels and stir.
Add the green peppers and carrots and stir well.
Keep stirring. Add the black pepper and keep stirring.
Once all the kernels are translucent and a savoury flavour is wafting in the air, take it off the heat. This might take 20 to 30 minutes.
Add the chopped green onions and serve hot.
chefTips: Translucent kernels and a savoury smell together are the doneness cue. Twenty to thirty minutes is the range and there is no shortcut.
Keep stirring throughout. Maize kernels catch easily and burnt maize is unpleasant.
Fresh maize off the cob, not tinned or frozen. The whole dish depends on the sweetness and moisture of fresh kernels.
Medium heat. High heat browns the outside of the kernels before they soften.
The green onions go in at the very end, off the heat.
Maize and kernel sizes vary, which is why several ingredients in the original carry no measurement — that is a deliberate choice about personal preference, not an omission.
The naturally meaty flavour is not marketing. Half an hour of slow cooking with garlic, ginger and tomato does produce it.
commonMistakes: Taking it off at ten minutes because the kernels look cooked.
Letting it catch on the bottom.
Adding the green onions during cooking.
sources: Adapted from Sophia Musoki, 'Sauteed Fresh From The Garden Maize (Corn)', A Kitchen In Uganda (25 August 2015) — the ingredient list, the method, the translucent-kernels-and-savoury-aroma doneness cue and the 20-to-30-minute window are hers.
She records it as her father's signature recipe, made only when there is an abundance of fresh maize, and describes the flavour as naturally meaty. Both are her words.

Her note that she gave no specific measurements for some ingredients because maize and kernel sizes vary and everyone has personal preferences is from the same post, which is why several quantities here are left open.
reheating: Warm in a pan with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Fresh maize supplies fibre, folate, thiamine and the carotenoids lutein and zeaxanthin.
Carrots, peppers and tomatoes make it a mixed-vegetable dish rather than a starch.
Plant-based, with only the frying oil added.
Substantial enough to eat as a main course.
culturalNote: Dishes that exist only during a glut are a real category in Ugandan cooking — fresh maize, termite mushrooms, banana blossoms, fresh beans. They are seasonal in a way that has nothing to do with menus and everything to do with what the garden has just produced too much of.
